correctness.rationale: For any existing finite affine plane q>=3, the incidence graph has point-line distances: point-point=2, intersecting line-line=2, parallel line-line=4 and nonincident point-line=3. At inclusive scale2 the Rips complex K is U∪V, where U is the all-points simplex with line cones, V is the join B of q-vertex discrete parallel classes with point cones, and U∩V is literally the incidence graph G. The equivariant inclusions identify H_*(U)=0 in positive degrees and H_q(V)=H_q(B), while Mayer–Vietoris gives natural integral H2(K)=H1(G) and Hq(K)=Hq(B), other reduced homology zero. The top join orientation changes sign when two classes are permuted, proving the collineation integral lattice or(C)⊗tensor_C ker(Z[C]→Z). This has rank (q-1)^(q+1), while the cycle lattice H1(G) has rank (q-1)^2(q+1). The natural flags-to-vertices exact sequence gives chi2=f_fixed_flags-f_fixed_points-f_fixed_lines+1. Factor-permutation trace is sign(pi_g) times product over cycles O of (number of lines fixed by g^|O| in one representative class -1), proving chi_q. For AG(2,q), a nonzero translation fixes no points or flags and q parallel lines, so character averaging on T of order q² gives quotient b2=0 and bq=[(q-1)^(q+1)+(q²-1)(q-1)(-1)^q]/q²; this is 0 at q3 but positive for q>=4. Independently evaluated cycle ranks, tensor ranks and quotient expression for q=3,4,5,7 (and parity boundaries), with q4 bq quotient18, q5 quotient160. These are algebraic checks; the all-affine-plane theorem rests on exact cover and equivariant Mayer–Vietoris.
risks: The q>=3 requirement is essential to distinguish homology degrees and to ensure the top join is at least simply connected.
Only the translation quotient of Desarguesian AG(2,q) for prime powers is claimed; arbitrary non-Desarguesian translation groups or integral quotient homology are outside scope.
